subject: Private Offer: hybrid SKU consolidation & channel passback flow
messages:
From: AegisHealth Procurement <procurement@aegishealth.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>, AcmeCloud Reseller <sales@acmecloud.io>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SKU consolidation and channel passback for private offer

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for taking time to review our marketplace plan. We have a hybrid commitment request: two metered SKUs (ingest + inference) and a small set of seat-based admin SKUs. Our procurement team would like to consolidate the metered SKUs into a single consumption SKU to simplify billing on our side and the marketplace listing.

Primary asks:
- Can Redwood consolidate the two metered SKUs into one usage SKU for the private offer?
- If yes, how will that affect the private-offer list price and the channel passback (we need clear %s for AcmeCloud as our reseller)?
- Will there be any metering latency or attribution differences we should expect?

We also need a term sheet draft and an updated SKU list to circulate internally by EOD Friday so our procurement/legal can start redlines.

Thanks,
Marcus Lee
Procurement Manager
AegisHealth

[Attachment: aegis_sku_list.xlsx]

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: Marcus Lee <procurement@aegishealth.com>
Cc: irene_choi@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com, AWS Marketplace Sales <aws-marketplace-sales@amazon.com>, AcmeCloud Reseller <sales@acmecloud.io>
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU consolidation and channel passback for private offer

On Wed, Jun 17, 2026 at 09:12 AM Marcus Lee <procurement@aegishealth.com> wrote:
> Thanks for taking time to review our marketplace plan. We have a hybrid commitment request...

Marcus — thanks for the clear asks and the SKU list. Short answers up front: yes, we can collapse the two metered SKUs into a single consumption SKU for the private offer; doing so is our recommended path for simplicity. There are a few trade-offs and ops details below.

Key implications:
- Pricing: We propose calculating the consolidated SKU list price by weighted-average of the two metered SKUs based on expected usage mix. That preserves the overall economics for Redwood while keeping a single line on Aegis' invoice.
- Channel passback: For AcmeCloud (your reseller), we can maintain an explicit passback % on the private offer. Standard practice is to set this as a fixed % of list price (e.g., 15%). If you need a gross-margin-first approach for the reseller, we can instead set a fixed dollar uplift per unit.
- Metering: There is no material metering latency change; attribution will be on the consolidated meter but we'll include metadata tags so you can break out ingest vs inference inside your usage export.

Next steps we suggest:
1) Redwood drafts a term sheet that includes the consolidated SKU, an example monthly invoice, and the proposed reseller passback % for AcmeCloud.
2) Ben (cc) will run a quick margin reflow to confirm net revenue implications for the consolidated SKU and for the reseller.
3) Irene (cc) can validate marketplace listing constraints for GCP/AWS if you plan to carry this as a single SKU across clouds.

I've attached a first-pass term sheet and a lightly annotated SKU mapping. If you can share an expected usage split for the two meters (even a rough 70/30), we'll produce the weighted price.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: RWI_priv_offer_term_sheet_v1.pdf]

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SKU consolidation and channel passback for private offer

Rishi / team — I ran a quick revenue reflow based on a 70/30 ingest:inference split (per Rishi's example). Notes:
- If list price = weighted avg, Redwood net effective AR after a 15% reseller passback and standard marketplace fees (~5%) is ~80% of list.
- If we instead set a fixed dollar uplift for reseller (to guarantee their absolute commission), Redwood net AR is slightly higher for high-usage customers but lower for low-usage.
- Tax treatment: marketplace-managed transacting vs direct private-offer invoicing has different tax flows. Laura, can you call out if Aegis' tax contact expects marketplace invoicing?

Recommendation: go with a 14% passback as a compromise; include a Gross-to-Net appendix in the term sheet.

-ben
Ben Carter
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi and team — this is helpful. Aegis prefers the fixed-% passback for bookkeeping simplicity; 14% is acceptable to our reseller, AcmeCloud, pending one operational ask: when the consolidated SKU is used, will the usage exports include a separate line item or tag for the original meters so we can internally allocate costs to our product teams?

Also, we need the term sheet updated to show:
- consolidated SKU name (Aegis-Consumption-v1)
- list price example at proposed usage tiers (monthly 0-500k tokens, 500k-2M, 2M+)
- explicit passback clause: 14% of list price to AcmeCloud monthly, paid by Redwood via marketplace settlement OR netted on invoice (please specify).

Can you get a revised term sheet and a sample invoice by EOD tomorrow? Our legal wants to start redlines Friday morning.

Best,
Marcus

AegisHealth
